S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S069.name: Intrusive_Symptoms
S069.description: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.

subtypes.Intrusive Memories: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Distressing Dreams: Recurrent distressing dreams in which the content and/or affect of the dream are related to the traumatic event.
subtypes.Dissociative Reactions (Flashbacks): Dissociative reactions (e.g., flashbacks) in which the individual feels or acts as if the traumatic event were recurring.
subtypes.Psychological Distress at Cues: Intense or prolonged psychological distress at exposure to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Physiological Reactions to Cues: Marked physiological reactions to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.

S070.name: Trauma_Avoidance
S070.description: Persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the traumatic event.

subtypes.Internal Avoidance: Efforts to avoid distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings about or closely associated with the traumatic event.
subtypes.External Avoidance: Efforts to avoid external reminders (people, places, conversations, activities, objects, situations) that arouse distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings.

S071.name: Trauma_Related_Amnesia
S071.description: Inability to remember an important aspect of the traumatic event (typically due to dissociative amnesia and not to other factors like head injury or alcohol).

subtypes.Fragmented Memory: Inability to recall only specific parts of the traumatic event while remembering others.
subtypes.Generalized Amnesia: Inability to recall the majority or the entirety of the traumatic event.

S074.name: Persistent_Negative_Emotional_State
S074.description: Persistent negative emotional state (e.g., fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame).

subtypes.Persistent Fear: A state of constant fear, anxiety, and tension.
subtypes.Persistent Horror: The shock and terror of the traumatic moment do not fade and remain.
subtypes.Persistent Anger: A state of chronic anger boiling inside or being expressed aggressively.
subtypes.Persistent Guilt: Unceasing feelings of guilt or remorse related to the trauma.
subtypes.Persistent Shame: Continuing to feel shame or humiliation due to the trauma.

S076.name: Inability_Positive_Emotions
S076.description: Persistent inability to experience positive emotions (e.g., inability to experience happiness, satisfaction, or loving feelings).

subtypes.Anhedonia for Happiness: Unable to feel happiness or joy even when good things happen.
subtypes.Lack of Satisfaction: Unable to experience satisfaction or pride even after achieving something good.
subtypes.Inability to Feel Love: Feeling numb to love or affection towards family or lovers.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where the mind feels empty and nothing is felt, as if all positive emotions are blocked.

S078.name: Reckless_Self_Destructive_Behavior
S078.description: Reckless or self-destructive behavior pattern that endangers one's safety or health.

subtypes.Risky Behaviors: Reckless actions disregarding consequences, such as speeding, dangerous sports, or criminal acts.
subtypes.Substance Abuse: Excessive drinking or drug use to harm oneself.
subtypes.Indisicriminate Sexual Behavior: Engaging in unprotected or dangerous sexual activities repetitively.
subtypes.Self-Harm: Actions that intentionally harm or scar one's own body.

S080.name: Exaggerated_Startle_Response
S080.description: Exaggerated startle response to minor stimuli.

subtypes.Auditory Startle: Startling excessively and flinching physically at sudden noises.
subtypes.Tactile Startle: Being extremely startled by unexpected physical contact.
subtypes.Visual Startle: Being greatly startled and wary of sudden appearances of people or rapid movements.
subtypes.Slow Recovery: Heart pounding and trembling for a long time after being startled, not calming down easily.

symptom.disease_info: Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) is a trauma- and stressor-related disorder that develops after exposure to actual or threatened death, serious injury, or sexual violence, either directly, as a witness, through learning of events to close others, or repeated exposure to aversive details. It is characterized by persistent re-experiencing of the trauma, avoidance of trauma-related cues, negative alterations in cognition and mood, and marked changes in arousal and reactivity lasting more than one month and causing significant distress or functional impairment. The course can be acute or chronic, with onset soon after the trauma or delayed, and it often fluctuates in intensity over time in response to reminders and ongoing stress. It is distinguished from other disorders such as depression or generalized anxiety by the clear temporal relationship to a qualifying traumatic event and the central role of trauma-linked re-experiencing and avoidance phenomena.

patient.personality: Jacqueline is a pragmatic, detail-focused tradesperson who prides herself on meticulous planning, hands-on mentoring, and a down-to-earth appreciation for nature, home cooking, and church community life.
patient.stressor: About fourteen months ago, Jacqueline was working with her crew on a commercial renovation when a section of unsecured ceiling grid and drywall collapsed, pinning her and a younger apprentice beneath heavy debris until firefighters extricated them. She remained conscious throughout, convinced she was going to die as she struggled to breathe under the weight and listened to her apprentice screaming nearby, and she later learned in the hospital that the apprentice had suffered life-threatening injuries. After being discharged with multiple fractures and soft-tissue injuries, she initially threw herself into managing her recovery plan and paperwork, but over the following months she became increasingly unable to return to job sites or even enter hardware stores without intense distress, straining her role as a foreman and mentor and leaving her husband to shoulder more financial and emotional burdens. As the year wore on and she found herself withdrawing from her gardening, church volunteering, and family interactions while taking growing risks on her snowmobile and on icy roads, her pastor and husband urged her to see a psychiatrist when she admitted that she felt numb and disconnected from any sense of joy or love in her life.
patient.chief_complaint: I feel like I just can’t feel happy or loving toward anyone anymore, no matter what I do.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.
S025.manifestation: I used to live for planning out jobs, tending my vegetable beds, and organizing church potlucks, but now even the thought of picking up a trowel or calling one of my crew just makes me feel blank and I end up sitting at the kitchen table staring at the paperwork instead.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: Most nights I lie there for hours replaying the accident in my head, and when I finally do drift off I jerk awake from these awful dreams about ceilings coming down, soaked in sweat and too wired and shaky to fall back asleep.

S069.name: Intrusive_Symptoms
S069.description: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.
S069.manifestation: Out of nowhere—like hearing a drill at the dentist or a board drop in the garage—it's like I'm right back under that ceiling grid, I can feel the weight on my chest and hear my apprentice screaming, and I freeze up or start crying because I can’t shut the pictures off in my mind.

S070.name: Trauma_Avoidance
S070.description: Persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the traumatic event.
S070.manifestation: I go out of my way to avoid anything that even smells like a job site, so I won’t drive past construction, I send my husband to the hardware store for the smallest thing, and I shut people down if they start talking about work, because if I let my mind go there I feel like I’m going to lose it.

S071.name: Trauma_Related_Amnesia
S071.description: Inability to remember an important aspect of the traumatic event (typically due to dissociative amnesia and not to other factors like head injury or alcohol).
S071.manifestation: I remember the start of the collapse and then being in the ambulance, but there are whole chunks in between—like what exactly happened when I was pinned or what I said to the firefighters—that I just can’t pull up no matter how hard I try, and it bothers me because it’s like my own memory has holes in it.

S074.name: Persistent_Negative_Emotional_State
S074.description: Persistent negative emotional state (e.g., fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame).
S074.manifestation: Most days I walk around with this heavy mix of dread and anger in my gut—angry at myself for not catching the bad rigging, scared something else is going to go wrong—and no matter what my husband or pastor says, I can’t shake the feeling that I failed that kid and that something terrible is always about to happen again.

S076.name: Inability_Positive_Emotions
S076.description: Persistent inability to experience positive emotions (e.g., inability to experience happiness, satisfaction, or loving feelings).
S076.manifestation: Even when my granddaughter runs up to me with a picture she drew or the church ladies throw me a little welcome-back coffee, I just feel flat and disconnected inside, like I’m watching someone else’s life and can’t actually feel the love or happiness I know I’m supposed to feel.

S078.name: Reckless_Self_Destructive_Behavior
S078.description: Reckless or self-destructive behavior pattern that endangers one's safety or health.
S078.manifestation: Lately I’ve been driving way too fast on icy back roads and taking my snowmobile out alone into bad conditions without caring if I flip it, and there are moments where I almost hope I’ll crash because at least then I’d feel something other than this numbness.

S080.name: Exaggerated_Startle_Response
S080.description: Exaggerated startle response to minor stimuli.
S080.manifestation: If a coworker drops a tool, a car backfires, or my husband just walks into the room without warning, I jump out of my skin—my heart pounds, my whole body tenses up, and it takes a long time before I can stop shaking and catch my breath again.
